newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania cabinet replaces privatisation managers.
newsitem.headline: Romania cabinet replaces privatisation managers.

text.p: Romania's government has replaced four representatives on the board of the country's main privatisation agency, the latest of several shake-ups denounced by the opposition as "political cleansing".
Four of five government representatives were replaced at the weekend by members of the National Peasant Party, the main party in the coalition elected last November.
Parliament's lower house last week appointed new members to the 17-member board of the State Ownership Fund (FPS), ousting representatives of the defeated Party of Social Democracy.
The government press office said its fifth representative had not yet been appointed.

The coalition government, made up of the Peasant Party, Social Democrats, other centrists and representatives of Romania's ethnic Hungarians, has pledged to speed up privatisation as part of free market reforms.
"The government is entitled to pursue its own policy," lower house chairman Ion Diaconescu said last week. "It cannot do so if the FPS is dominated by the former ruling party."

Local media said the whole FPS board -- made up of the junior minister for privatisation plus appointees from parliament, the presidency and the government -- would be replaced by the end of the month.

The FPS has been accused of stalling selloff of equity in some 6,500 companies in its administration. It has been put under scrutiny over alleged irregularities by undervaluing the capital of some of the 3,000 companies it has turned private.
The Fund declined to comment on the new appointments.
